title: A standard smooth presentation can be chosen to include given elements as generators
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $A$ a standard smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], $n\ge0$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n\in A$ (not necessarily distinct). Then there are integers $m\ge0$ and $c$ with $n\le c\le n+m$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+m}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+m}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ sending the class of $x_i$ to $a_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n$, such that the image in $A$ of $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] is a unit of $A$; that is, a standard smooth presentation of $A$ over $R$ whose first $n$ variables map to $a_1,\dots,a_n$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694) and its proof (lines 705-718: presentation R[x_1..x_n,y_1..y_m]/(x_1-h_1,...,x_n-h_n,g_1,...,g_d), c = n+d). Stacks states it for a finite subset E of order n; the proof is verbatim the same for a family a_1..a_n with repetitions, which is the form used here

proof.text: (A standard smooth presentation of $A$.) Since $A$ is standard smooth [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], there are integers $m\ge d\ge0$, polynomials $g_1,\dots,g_d\in R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha_0:R[y_1,\dots,y_m]/(g_1,\dots,g_d)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ such that, writing $\pi_0:R[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to A$ for the composite of the quotient map and $\alpha_0$, the element $\pi_0(\Delta_0)$ is a unit of $A$, where $\Delta_0=\det(\partial g_j/\partial y_i)_{1\le i,j\le d}\in R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. The map $\pi_0$ is surjective and its kernel is $(g_1,\dots,g_d)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694), proof lines 705-718

proof.text: (Lifts of the $a_i$.) Since $\pi_0$ is surjective, choose $h_1,\dots,h_n\in R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ with $\pi_0(h_i)=a_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n$ (if $a_i=a_k$ the lifts may be chosen independently; nothing below uses distinctness).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694), proof lines 705-718

proof.text: (The new polynomial ring and the map to $A$.) Let $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_m]$, a polynomial ring in $n+m$ variables, ordered $z_1,\dots,z_{n+m}=x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_m$ (so $z_k=x_k$ for $k\le n$ and $z_{n+k}=y_k$ for $k\le m$); regard $R[y_1,\dots,y_m]\subset P$ as the polynomials involving no $x_k$. By the universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] there is a unique $R$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:P\to A$ with $\varphi(x_i)=a_i$ ($i\le n$) and $\varphi(y_k)=\pi_0(y_k)$ ($k\le m$). Its restriction to $R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ agrees with $\pi_0$ on every $y_k$, hence equals $\pi_0$ (uniqueness part of the universal property). Therefore $\varphi(x_i-h_i)=a_i-\pi_0(h_i)=0$, $\varphi(g_j)=\pi_0(g_j)=0$, and $\varphi$ is surjective since already $\pi_0=\varphi|_{R[y]}$ is.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694), proof lines 705-718

proof.text: (The kernel of $\varphi$.) Let $J=(x_1-h_1,\dots,x_n-h_n)\subset P$ and $I=J+(g_1,\dots,g_d)P$. We show $\ker\varphi=I$. By Step 3, $I\subset\ker\varphi$. Conversely, let $\sigma:P\to R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ be the $R$-algebra homomorphism with $\sigma(x_i)=h_i$, $\sigma(y_k)=y_k$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The set $T=\{F\in P: F-\sigma(F)\in J\}$ contains $R$ (as $\sigma$ is the identity on constants), each $y_k$ ($y_k-\sigma(y_k)=0$) and each $x_i$ ($x_i-h_i\in J$), and is closed under sums and under products, since $FG-\sigma(F)\sigma(G)=F\,(G-\sigma(G))+\sigma(G)\,(F-\sigma(F))$; as $P$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by the $x_i$ and $y_k$, $T=P$. Now let $F\in\ker\varphi$. Since $F-\sigma(F)\in J\subset\ker\varphi$, $\pi_0(\sigma(F))=\varphi(\sigma(F))=\varphi(F)=0$, so $\sigma(F)\in\ker\pi_0=(g_1,\dots,g_d)R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ (Step 1: $\alpha_0$ is injective), which lies in $I$. Hence $F=(F-\sigma(F))+\sigma(F)\in J+I=I$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694), proof lines 705-718 (the source writes the presentation A = R[x,y]/(x_i - h_i, g_j) without proof; the elimination of the x_i is written out here)

proof.text: (The new presentation.) By Steps 3 and 4 and the homomorphism theorem, $\varphi$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:P/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ sending the class of $x_i$ to $a_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. Set $c=n+d$ and $(f_1,\dots,f_c)=(x_1-h_1,\dots,x_n-h_n,g_1,\dots,g_d)$, so $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. From $0\le d\le m$ we get $n\le c\le n+m$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694), proof lines 705-718

proof.text: (The partial derivatives.) By the monomial formula of [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative], for $H\in R[y_1,\dots,y_m]\subset P$ we have $\partial H/\partial x_k=0$ for every $k\le n$ (no monomial of $H$ contains $x_k$), and $\partial H/\partial y_i$ computed in $P$ equals $\partial H/\partial y_i$ computed in $R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$. Together with $\partial x_j/\partial x_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\partial x_j/\partial y_i=0$ this gives, for the variables $z_1,\dots,z_c=x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_d$: $\partial f_j/\partial x_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\partial f_{n+j'}/\partial x_k=\partial g_{j'}/\partial x_k=0$ for $k,j\le n$, $j'\le d$; $\partial f_j/\partial y_i=-\partial h_j/\partial y_i$ and $\partial f_{n+j'}/\partial y_i=\partial g_{j'}/\partial y_i$ for $i,j'\le d$, $j\le n$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694), proof lines 705-718

proof.text: (The Jacobian determinant.) By Step 6, the $c\times c$ matrix $M=(\partial f_j/\partial z_k)_{1\le k,j\le c}$ (rows indexed by the variables, columns by the relations, as in [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]) is in block form $M=\begin{pmatrix}1_n&0\\C&G\end{pmatrix}$ with $1_n$ the $n\times n$ identity (rows and columns $1,\dots,n$), upper right $n\times d$ block zero ($\partial g_{j'}/\partial x_k=0$), $C=(-\partial h_j/\partial y_i)_{i\le d,\,j\le n}$ and $G=(\partial g_{j'}/\partial y_i)_{1\le i,j'\le d}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-block-triangular-determinant] (with $p=n$, $q=d$), $\det M=\det 1_n\cdot\det G=\Delta_0$, an element of $R[y_1,\dots,y_m]\subset P$. Its image in $A$ under $P\to P/I\xrightarrow{\alpha}A$, which is $\varphi$, is $\varphi(\Delta_0)=\pi_0(\Delta_0)$ (Step 3), a unit of $A$ by Step 1.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EY (lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators, line 694), proof lines 705-718 (the source sets c = n + d and leaves the Jacobian computation to the reader; it is written out here)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The integers $m$ and $c$ with $n\le c\le n+m$ (Step 5), the polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[z_1,\dots,z_{n+m}]=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_m]$ and the isomorphism $\alpha:R[z_1,\dots,z_{n+m}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, which sends the class of $z_i=x_i$ to $a_i$ for $i\le n$ (Step 5) and maps $\det(\partial f_j/\partial z_i)_{i,j\le c}$ to a unit (Step 7), form a standard smooth presentation of $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] as claimed.

split_report.summary: Split following the proof of Stacks 07EY (smoothing.tex lines 705-718), read in full; tag 07EY checked in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (line 9463, smoothing-lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators). Eight steps: a standard smooth presentation R[y_1..y_m]/(g_1..g_d) with unit Jacobian determinant Delta_0 (Step 1), lifts h_i of a_i (Step 2), the map phi: R[x,y] -> A with x_i -> a_i (Step 3), ker phi = (x_i - h_i, g_j) by the substitution sigma: x_i -> h_i (Step 4, written out; the source states the presentation without proof), c = n + d with n <= c <= n + m from d <= m (Step 5), the partial derivatives from the monomial formula (Step 6), the block lower-triangular Jacobian [[1_n, 0], [C, G]] with determinant Delta_0 by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-block-triangular-determinant (Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₁₂) (Step 7), conclusion (Step 8). Statement unchanged (it already treats a family a_1..a_n with repetitions, as the citers lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-base Step 2 and lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-weak Step 4 use it; both use exactly the statement: the presentation over the base with c relations, n <= c <= n+m, unit Jacobian of the first c variables, x_i -> a_i). lean.statement: theorem exists_standardSmoothPresentation_include_generators {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsStandardSmooth R A] (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → A) : ∃ (m c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ n + m) (P : SubmersivePresentation R A (Fin (n + m)) (Fin c)), n ≤ c ∧ P.map = Fin.castLE hc ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, P.val (Fin.castAdd m i) = a i

reviewed_lean.note: R, A commutative, IsStandardSmooth; family a : Fin n → A with repetitions; m, c with n ≤ c ≤ n+m; presentation = Mathlib SubmersivePresentation on Fin (n+m) / Fin c with map = Fin.castLE hc (Jacobian in the first c variables, unit) and val (castAdd i) = a i; this replaces the inline quotient and det
